Coding agents are fast, but they start before you've agreed on the approach and finish with changes nobody really reviewed. Coppice puts the agent CLIs you already use (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Kilo Code) on a ticket board on your own machine, with no Coppice account. Hire specialists. Keep the final say.

## In this release

- **Automatic updates.** Coppice checks for new versions in the background. On Linux, installing the `.deb` adds Coppice's package source, so new versions arrive with your other updates in Software Updater, or with `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade`. On macOS, a banner tells you when a new version is out. To turn checks off, open **Settings → Updates** and turn off **Automatic updates**.
- **Use your own API key or another provider.** Want your own API key, or a model your CLI doesn't offer? Use OpenCode: run `opencode`, type `/connect`, pick your provider and paste your key. OpenCode keeps the key, and Coppice never asks for it. Then set an agent's **Connector** to **OpenCode** and pick a model. See [Providers](https://getcoppice.app/docs/providers#use-your-own-api-key-or-another-provider).
- **Refresh models finds new providers.** If you added a provider while Coppice was open, click **Refresh models** and it shows up under **Model**. No restart.
- **A short setup on first run.** A fresh install adds your first repository, board and starter team. You can reopen it from Tools.
- **Chat with Cursor and Kilo Code.** Every CLI can chat now. Chats on CLIs Coppice can't keep read-only show a banner.
- **Diagrams in plans.** For flows, architecture or data models, a plan may include a small diagram. The written plan is always there too.
- **Your own keyboard shortcuts.** Change any shortcut under `[keybindings]` in Settings.
- **Review rounds stop at three.** After three rounds of review on a ticket, it waits for you instead of going around again.
